dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Basic Graph Theory » Connectivity
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Let $ G $ be a graph and let $ T\subseteq V(G) $ such that for any pair $ u,v\in T $ there are $ 2k $ edge-disjoint paths from $ u $ to $ v $ in $ G $ . Then $ G $ contains $ k $ edge-disjoint trees, each of which contains $ T $ .
dossier_meta.context_text: This problem was featured as unsolved problem #22 in Bondy and Murty's book "Graph Theory" [BM]. See also a posting on the open problem forum of the Egerváry Research Group on Combinatorial Optimization.
dossier_meta.references_text: - [BM] J. A. Bondy and U. S. R. Murty. Graph theory, volume 244 of Graduate Texts in Mathematics. Springer, New York, 2008.
